messages:
maria: Heads-up — we're rolling an RBAC change tomorrow that tightens who can restore backups and introduces new KMS key constraints. Need alignment on audit logging and an emergency restore playbook.
kevin: Which systems are in scope? RDS snapshots, S3 backups, MinIO? Also is this tied to the CMK rotation?
dinesh: Also want to know if this would've prevented the last failed-restore incident (INC-2026-102). We need to avoid locking on-call out.
maria: In-scope: Postgres RDS/EBS snapshots, S3 backup bucket (SSE-KMS), internal MinIO object-store snapshots, and archived vault snapshots. Security plans a CMK rotation next week — we want least-privilege policies before rotation.
jordan: For KMS we can require EncryptionContext checks on decrypt ops, e.g. require kms:EncryptionContext:redwood:backup == <backup-id> so only tagged restores can use the key. Also emit context in audit logs.
claire: Compliance: retention for audit logs must be >= 1 year and immutable. Any RBAC change needs a documented attestation and key-access review logs. Legal hold must be considered.
kevin: Draft IAM/KMS policy example for the restore service role — give kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey only for the CMK used by backups. Example snippet: ```json
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-...",
  "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"kms:EncryptionContext:redwood:purpose": "backup-restore"}}
}
```
maria: Good. For emergency break-glass, we need a time-limited bypass process (3-step: approval via PD incident, temporary policy attach, explicit audit entry). Who owns the runbook?
dinesh: I'll own the runbook update. Suggest a default role name restore-service-role and a separate emergency role restore-emergency-role with MFA & PD approval required. Also ensure CloudTrail is logging KMS API events and S3 data events for GetObject.
kevin: Quick test command to simulate decryption locally: ```bash
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob.enc --key-id alias/redwood-backups --encryption-context purpose=backup-restore --query Plaintext --output text | base64 --decode
```
Use in staging first.
kms-bot: Scheduled rotation: cmk-backups will rotate key material on 2026-03-25T02:00:00Z. Admins: @maria @kevin notified.
jordan: Alerting proposals: - create detection rule for kms:Decrypt failures (rate threshold) - alert on unauthorized kms:Decrypt calls - alert on sudden spike in snapshot restores. Send to secur-ops PD.
claire: Add requirement: export audit logs to compliance-archive bucket (write-only, locked) and produce monthly access review reports.
maria: Proposed playbook (short): 1) Pre-change: export last 30d audit logs, snapshot RBAC configs, dry-run on staging. 2) Deployment: apply policy canary to 10% org units, monitor decrypt errors and S3 GetObject errors for 1h. 3) Rollback: auto-revert if restore error rate > 2x baseline or PD escalation. 4) Emergency: restore-emergency-role attach + annotate audit log with incident id.
dinesh: I'll add staging test cases: restore small snapshot, restore large snapshot, object-restore rate limit, key-rotation simulation.
kevin: I'll open PR with policy change + tests and link the runbook: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/5821 (WIP). Please review before EOD. :thumbsup:
maria: Thanks. I will export today's audit logs and create the attestation doc for compliance. Ping me for a dry-run — plan to cut the change at 2026-03-24 04:00 UTC so rotation doesn't collide.
claire: Reminder: keep evidence for 730 days for legal holds.
maria: Closing — great sync. If anyone sees a spike in KMS errors tomorrow, @dinesh take lead and follow playbook. :heavy_check_mark:
